## Investigation summary

**Bottom line:** I found one root cause. The degradation originates in `ts-station-service`, specifically its database access path for the `ts.station` table (pod `ts-station-service-646c8dc9f-glgfp`). Slow station queries hold up callers, and the latency propagates upstream to the user-facing endpoints.

### Affected endpoints and services (abnormal vs. normal)

| Service | Normal avg / p95 | Abnormal avg / p95 | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts-station-service | 1.2 / 2.8 ms | 98.5 / 423 ms (max 3.3 s) | **origin** |
| ts-basic-service | 7.2 / 16.6 ms | 62.9 / 420 ms | propagation |
| ts-route-plan-service | 27 / 64 ms | 117 / 457 ms | propagation |
| ts-travel-plan-service | 42 / 102 ms | 168 / 477 ms | propagation |
| ts-travel-service | 6.7 / 23 ms | 30 / 224 ms | propagation |
| ts-travel2-service | 6.4 / 21 ms | 25 / 221 ms | propagation |
| ts-admin-basic-info-service | 6.1 / 10 ms | 82 / 631 ms | propagation |
| ts-admin-route-service | 8.9 / 15 ms | 34 / 219 ms | propagation |
| ts-ui-dashboard / loadgenerator | ~20–21 ms | ~30–31 ms (max ~3.4 s) | user-facing symptom |

No services show HTTP 5xx responses. Services such as auth, order, route, train, user, verification, price, and config are unchanged.
